args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1, checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 had already been unhealthy in staging (v2.3.1-rc). Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001.

1. **Diagnosis:** The latest version, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging before it went to production.
2. **Rollback:** All three regions now run v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-ups, and it paged the on-call engineer. The first request to create it timed out. The incident list showed it had been created anyway, so I didn't send it again. That means there's only one incident and one page.

The incident lists two follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that failed in staging was still promoted to production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
